arguments.title: Replace capture-hook-stdin.sh wrapper with first-class tracing file logging in session-capture-hook
arguments.description:
## Objective
Debug why the Copilot session capture hook produces no output, and remove the
`tools/agent-hooks/capture-hook-stdin.sh` bash wrapper in favor of first-class
`tracing` file logging inside the `session-capture-hook` Rust binary.

## Root cause findings
1. `.vscode/settings.json` no longer sets `chat.hookFilesLocations`
   (removed in commit `edf2f508` "remove vscode workspace settings"), so VS
   Code never loads `.github/hooks/hooks.json` at all — no hook fires
   regardless of the wrapper. This is the primary reason no capture has been
   produced since 2026-08-13.
2. Independent of (1), `tools/agent-hooks/capture-hook-stdin.sh` has no
   structured logging: failures (missing binary, bad json, mkdir/mv errors)
   are only visible via a stray `.session/local/hook-captures/<event>.json`
   file or a stderr line, with no timestamped trail.

## Plan
- Add `tracing`/`tracing-subscriber`/`tracing-appender` to
  `memory-api/crates/session-capture-hook` and log every stage (stdin read,
  parsed event, transcript resolution, persisted plan, errors) to
  `.session/local/logs/session-capture-hook.log`.
- Delete `tools/agent-hooks/capture-hook-stdin.sh`; point
  `.github/hooks/hooks.json` directly at the `session-capture-hook` binary
  (PATH-resolved, with a `CARGO_HOME` fallback baked into the command).
- Update `.agents/instructions/session/worktree-provisioning.instructions.md`
  and `tools/agent-hooks/SUBAGENT_RUN_CAPTURE.md` to describe the new log file
  instead of the removed capture-directory convention.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `cargo build -p session-capture-hook` succeeds with the new tracing deps.
2. `tools/agent-hooks/capture-hook-stdin.sh` no longer exists and no
   `.github/hooks/hooks.json` entry references it.
3. Running the binary with `--from-hook-stdin` writes a log line to
   `.session/local/logs/session-capture-hook.log` for a sample hook payload.
4. Docs referencing the old wrapper/capture-directory are updated.

# Sub-Agent Run Capture

`SubagentStart` and `SubagentStop` are captured by invoking the
`session-capture-hook` binary directly with `--from-hook-stdin` (see
`.github/hooks/hooks.json`). The hook logs each stage to
`.session/local/logs/session-capture-hook.log` and persists the lifecycle
event in the parent session's `events.json`. The persisted event is keyed by
the parent session id and `agent_id`; it retains `agent_type`, the hook
timestamp, and the stop state.

replacements.oldString:
The binary usage is:

```text
Usage: session-capture-hook (session sync ingest) [--from-hook-stdin] [--transcript-path <PATH>] [--store-root <PATH>] [--workspace-slug <SLUG>] [--trigger <NAME>]
```

The hook writes `{}` to stdout for both success and early skip, with diagnostics only on stderr. There is no hook log file, so an externally silent success is indistinguishable from a silent skip.

## Hook Events

| Event | Registered command | Timeout |
|---|---|---:|
| `SessionStart` | `bash tools/agent-hooks/capture-hook-stdin.sh` | 300s |
| `UserPromptSubmit` | `bash tools/agent-hooks/capture-hook-stdin.sh` | 300s |
| `PreToolUse` | `bash tools/agent-hooks/rtk-hook-copilot.sh`, then `bash tools/agent-hooks/preflight-write.sh` | 5s, 30s |
| `PostToolUse` | `bash tools/agent-hooks/validate-docs.sh`, `bash tools/agent-hooks/terminal-pwd.sh`, then `bash tools/agent-hooks/capture-hook-stdin.sh` | 30s, 5s, 120s |
| `Stop` | `bash tools/agent-hooks/capture-hook-stdin.sh` | 120s |

[capture-hook-stdin.sh](../../../tools/agent-hooks/capture-hook-stdin.sh) records the raw hook stdin payload to `.session/local/hook-captures/<event>.json` (gitignored, one file per event, latest write wins) and then forwards the identical bytes to `session-capture-hook --from-hook-stdin`. It replaced a bare `tee ./session.log | session-capture-hook --from-hook-stdin` command: hook commands are not run through a POSIX shell on Windows, so `tee` resolved to PowerShell's `Tee-Object` and wrote a UTF-16LE BOM with zero payload bytes. Set `SESSION_HOOK_CAPTURE=0` to suppress the capture while still forwarding.
replacements.newString:
The binary usage is:

```text
Usage: session-capture-hook (session sync ingest) [--from-hook-stdin] [--transcript-path <PATH>] [--store-root <PATH>] [--workspace-slug <SLUG>] [--trigger <NAME>]
```

The hook writes `{}` to stdout for both success and early skip, with human diagnostics on stderr and a structured `tracing` trail in
`.session/local/logs/session-capture-hook.log` (gitignored, appended across invocations, never rotated). Set `SESSION_HOOK_LOG_DIR` to relocate the log directory and `SESSION_HOOK_LOG` (or `RUST_LOG`) to change the filter level (default `info`); use `debug` to see every parsed field and decision branch.

## Hook Events

| Event | Registered command | Timeout |
|---|---|---:|
| `SessionStart` | `session-capture-hook --from-hook-stdin` | 300s |
| `UserPromptSubmit` | `session-capture-hook --from-hook-stdin` | 300s |
| `PreToolUse` | `bash tools/agent-hooks/rtk-hook-copilot.sh`, then `bash tools/agent-hooks/preflight-write.sh` | 5s, 30s |
| `PostToolUse` | `bash tools/agent-hooks/validate-docs.sh`, `bash tools/agent-hooks/terminal-pwd.sh`, then `session-capture-hook --from-hook-stdin` | 30s, 5s, 120s |
| `Stop` | `session-capture-hook --from-hook-stdin` | 120s |

Each registration in [hooks.json](../../../.github/hooks/hooks.json) invokes the binary directly (`bash -c 'PATH="$PATH:${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin" session-capture-hook --from-hook-stdin'`), so `session-capture-hook` need not already be on the hook environment's `PATH`. The previous `tools/agent-hooks/capture-hook-stdin.sh` wrapper — which persisted raw stdin to `.session/local/hook-captures/<event>.json` before forwarding it — was removed; its diagnostic role is now served by the binary's own `tracing` file log, and its `SESSION_HOOK_CAPTURE`/`SESSION_HOOK_CAPTURE_DIR` env vars no longer apply.

# Sub-Agent Run Capture

`SubagentStart` and `SubagentStop` are captured by invoking the
`session-capture-hook` binary directly with `--from-hook-stdin` (see
`.github/hooks/hooks.json`). The hook logs each stage to
`.session/local/logs/session-capture-hook.log` and persists the lifecycle
event in the parent session's `events.json`. The persisted event is keyed by
the parent session id and `agent_id`; it retains `agent_type`, the hook
timestamp, and the stop state.

The binary usage is:

```text
Usage: session-capture-hook (session sync ingest) [--from-hook-stdin] [--transcript-path <PATH>] [--store-root <PATH>] [--workspace-slug <SLUG>] [--trigger <NAME>]
```

The hook writes `{}` to stdout for both success and early skip, with diagnostics only on stderr. There is no hook log file, so an externally silent success is indistinguishable from a silent skip.

| Event | Registered command | Timeout |
|---|---|---:|
| `SessionStart` | `bash tools/agent-hooks/capture-hook-stdin.sh` | 300s |
| `UserPromptSubmit` | `bash tools/agent-hooks/capture-hook-stdin.sh` | 300s |
| `PreToolUse` | `bash tools/agent-hooks/rtk-hook-copilot.sh`, then `bash tools/agent-hooks/preflight-write.sh` | 5s, 30s |
| `PostToolUse` | `bash tools/agent-hooks/validate-docs.sh`, `bash tools/agent-hooks/terminal-pwd.sh`, then `bash tools/agent-hooks/capture-hook-stdin.sh` | 30s, 5s, 120s |
| `Stop` | `bash tools/agent-hooks/capture-hook-stdin.sh` | 120s |

[capture-hook-stdin.sh](../../../tools/agent-hooks/capture-hook-stdin.sh) records the raw hook stdin payload to `.session/local/hook-captures/<event>.json` (gitignored, one file per event, latest write wins) and then forwards the identical bytes to `session-capture-hook --from-hook-stdin`. It replaced a bare `tee ./session.log | session-capture-hook --from-hook-stdin` command: hook commands are not run through a POSIX shell on Windows, so `tee` resolved to PowerShell's `Tee-Object` and wrote a UTF-16LE BOM with zero payload bytes. The fix is probably to only initialize file logging from the actual `main()` binary entrypoint rather than the shared library logic, or to gate it behind an env var so tests can disable it. I should check the fixture harness to see whether it spawns the compiled binary as a subprocess or calls the logic directly, and how existing tests scope paths like temp directories.

events.reasoning_text:
The test spawns the actual binary with cwd set to a fixture directory, so our new log directory write under the default relative path lands inside `.session/local`, which breaks the "no mutation" assertion for SessionStart. I need to either change the default log directory so it doesn't live under `.session/local` relative to cwd, or update the tests to permit that new file.

Since the invariant that session records shouldn't create side files in the main checkout is a real product guarantee, the better fix is to default the log directory to somewhere outside the repo entirely, like the system temp directory (`std::env::temp_dir().join("session-capture-hook")`), keeping SESSION_HOOK_LOG_DIR as an override. This avoids polluting any checkout regardless of cwd and works portably across platforms, so I'll implement that and update the docs.

## Summary

**Root cause of "hook doesn't work":** commit `edf2f508` ("remove vscode workspace settings") deleted `chat.hookFilesLocations` from [.vscode/settings.json](.vscode/settings.json), so VS Code stopped loading [.github/hooks/hooks.json](.github/hooks/hooks.json) entirely — no hook fired regardless of the wrapper. Restored just that key, per your choice.

**Wrapper removal + first-class logging**, per your request:
- Deleted `tools/agent-hooks/capture-hook-stdin.sh`.
- [.github/hooks/hooks.json](.github/hooks/hooks.json): all 7 registrations now call `session-capture-hook --from-hook-stdin` directly via `bash -c 'PATH="$PATH:${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin" session-capture-hook --from-hook-stdin'` (keeps the cargo-bin PATH fallback the old script had, drops the jq/mktemp/mv machinery).
- Added `tracing`/`tracing-subscriber`/`tracing-appender` to [session-capture-hook/Cargo.toml](memory-api/crates/session-capture-hook/Cargo.toml) and a new [logging.rs](memory-api/crates/session-capture-hook/src/logging.rs) that writes a structured, file-only log (stdout/stderr stay reserved for the hook contract) to the OS temp dir (`session-capture-hook/session-capture-hook.log`, overridable via `SESSION_HOOK_LOG_DIR`, filter via `SESSION_HOOK_LOG`/`RUST_LOG`) — deliberately outside any `.session` checkout tree so logging can never trip the "hook must not mutate the session store" invariant.
- Instrumented [main.rs](memory-api/crates/session-capture-hook/src/main.rs) and [args.rs](memory-api/crates/session-capture-hook/src/args.rs) with `tracing` events at every decision point (invocation, parsed args, stdin length, store-root resolution, skip reasons, persisted plan).
- Updated [worktree-provisioning.instructions.md](.agents/instructions/session/worktree-provisioning.instructions.md) and [SUBAGENT_RUN_CAPTURE.md](tools/agent-hooks/SUBAGENT_RUN_CAPTURE.md) to describe the new invocation and log location instead of the removed wrapper/capture-directory convention.

Verified: `cargo build -p session-capture-hook` and `cargo test -p session-capture-hook` (29 tests) pass; manual run of the exact `hooks.json` command against a fixture payload writes a structured log line and correctly reproduces the "no worktree assignment" failure mode from a related ticket — now visible instead of silent.

Note: I couldn't create/update a tracking ticket via ticket-mcp because this ad-hoc debugging session has no session-store worktree assignment (the same class of bug just diagnosed) — you may want to file one manually for the record.

events.reasoning_text:
I found it: session ids must now be UUIDs per the refactor ticket, which rejects slug-shaped ids. My test used non-UUID ids like "missed-start-{unique_suffix}", and I notice other existing tests also use non-UUID ids like "fresh-session-{}" or "different-session" — so I need to check how those are handled.

Those other tests only check that no worktree gets created, they never go through SessionWorkspaceResolver.resolve(), which is the part that strictly validates UUID format. Provisioning itself (creating the .worktrees/<id> directory) doesn't enforce UUID format — only resolve_capture_store_root's call to resolver.resolve() does — so my test just needs to use a proper UUID session id to work correctly.

I'll fix my test by swapping the non-UUID session id for a fixed valid UUID literal, matching the pattern used in neighboring tests, since tempdir isolation already makes a hardcoded UUID safe to reuse.

arguments.explanation: Correct stale doc claiming UserPromptSubmit is the primary provisioning trigger, and document the new lazy-provisioning fallback

replacements.newString: `SessionStart` is the event eager provisioning is primarily attached to, so a session receives an isolated worktree before its first prompt. If `SessionStart` was missed for a session (e.g. hooks were reconfigured mid-session, or the event never fired), the hook lazily provisions instead on the first later event that carries a session id and isn't `Stop` (`UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `SubagentStart`, `SubagentStop`) — `Stop` intentionally never provisions, so a session that never began capturing does not spring a fresh worktree into existence only at its end. The `UserPromptSubmit` timeout is 300 seconds to allow a cold provision.
replacements.oldString: `UserPromptSubmit` is the event eager provisioning is attached to, so a session receives an isolated worktree before implementation begins. `SessionStart` also fires before the first tool call but is capture-only; provisioning deliberately waits for a prompt. The `UserPromptSubmit` timeout is 300 seconds to allow a cold provision.

replacements.newString: Eager provisioning runs for `SessionStart` with a non-blank session id, plus a lazy fallback on any other non-`Stop` event when no assignment is resolvable (see "What Fires And When"). A successful provision creates the session worktree; worktree discovery is positional from the supported directory layouts, with no main-checkout session-to-worktree assignment index. `WORKTREE_EAGER_PROVISION` is opt-out: the condition treats unset as enabled and only `0` as disabled.
replacements.oldString: Eager provisioning runs only for `UserPromptSubmit` with a non-blank session id. A successful provision creates the session worktree; worktree discovery is positional from the supported directory layouts, with no main-checkout session-to-worktree assignment index. `WORKTREE_EAGER_PROVISION` is opt-out: the condition treats unset as enabled and only `0` as disabled.

arguments.newString: Eager provisioning runs for `SessionStart` with a non-blank session id, plus a lazy fallback on any other non-`Stop` event when no assignment is resolvable (see "What Fires And When"). A successful provision creates the session worktree and writes a minimal registration record — `session_id`, `metadata.worktree.{path,branch,allocation_mode,status}` — to the **main checkout's own** `.session/sessions/<session-uuid>/session.json` via `SessionStoreConfig::register_provisioned_worktree` (ticket 842d74cb D1: the main checkout is the authoritative session-to-worktree registry). This is a no-op once a record with a worktree assignment already exists, so it never clobbers a real capture. Worktree discovery is otherwise positional from the supported directory layouts. `WORKTREE_EAGER_PROVISION` is opt-out: the condition treats unset as enabled and only `0` as disabled.

It reads the worktree's own just-captured `metadata.worktree` and mirrors it into the main checkout's registry via the existing `register_provisioned_worktree`, best-effort and idempotent.
